stories.title: On-Pi service-control CLI -- stop/start/restart/kill/status each OBD service or ALL (maintenance tool)
acceptance: a CLI utility on the Pi (e.g. scripts/obdctl.sh + a `make`/deploy-installed entrypoint) run as `obdctl <action> <service|all>`; actions: status, start, stop, restart, kill (SIGKILL for a stuck unit). Bare/no-arg invocation = status of ALL (never a destructive default). --help + --dry-run.

CANONICAL UNIT LIST (SSOT, grounded -- the 8 deploy-installed OBD-project units, verified on the Pi 2026-07-27): eclipse-obd, eclipse-powerwatch, eclipse-states-http, eclipse-boot-state, eclipse-dashboard, rfcomm-bind, splash-boot, splash-grace. Derive/share the list from a single source (extend the US-403 service_control.py SERVICE_ALLOWLIST or a shared manifest) so it does NOT drift from what deploy installs -- do NOT hardcode a second divergent list.
short aliases accepted (e.g. `obd`, `powerwatch`, `dashboard`, `states`, `splash`) + the full unit name; `all` targets every unit in the canonical list

SAFETY -- eclipse-powerwatch is the safe-shutdown guard (D-7/F-7 cardinal rule: never leave it stopped or shutdown protection is disabled). stop/kill of powerwatch (directly or via `all`) prints a LOUD warning + requires an explicit confirm (or a --force/--yes flag); restart/status of powerwatch is unrestricted. The tool must make it easy to see powerwatch is down + to bring it back.

SAFETY -- `kill` (SIGKILL) is forceful: require explicit intent (confirm or explicit action word), never a fallback of `stop`; document that kill can leave a unit's resources uncleaned (use stop first, kill only when stuck)

`all` acts in a SENSIBLE ORDER: stop/kill in reverse-dependency order (kiosk/emitters/splash first, then states-http, then the core eclipse-obd/powerwatch last); start in dependency order (states-http before dashboard, etc.) -- avoid races + orphaned kiosks

HONEST OUTPUT: for each targeted unit print before-state -> action -> after-state (active/inactive/failed/not-installed) + a clear per-unit OK/FAIL; `all` prints a summary table; a not-installed unit is reported honestly, not an error-crash; non-zero exit if any requested action failed
privilege handled cleanly (systemctl needs root -- sudo or the existing 51-eclipse-service-control polkit path); the tool tells the operator if it lacks privilege rather than failing cryptically
deploy-installed (deploy-pi.sh) so it's on the Pi after a deploy, on PATH or a known location; documented in deploy/README + a one-line usage in --help
bash -n / shellcheck clean (or ruff if Python); a test exercises the action-dispatch + the canonical-list-vs-deploy-installed consistency + the powerwatch-stop-guard

validationCriteria.action: on the Pi: obdctl status all
validationCriteria.outcome: lists all 8 OBD units with their live state; no crash on any not-installed unit
eclipse-obd restarts; before->after state shown; exit 0
stops the units in reverse-dependency order; powerwatch stop triggers the loud warning + confirm; summary table shows per-unit result
requires explicit intent, SIGKILLs the kiosk, reports killed + after-state inactive
refuses/warns + requires confirm (safe-shutdown-guard protection); restart powerwatch is unrestricted

conditionalOutcomes: if enumerating the canonical unit list from the deploy scripts vs service_control.py reveals a drift (a unit deploy installs that neither list knows), reconcile to ONE SSOT + flag it -- do not silently maintain two lists

eclipse-sync.service appears in the US-403 allow-list but was NOT in the Pi's installed units (2026-07-27) -- confirm whether it's a real unit or folded into eclipse-obd; include only actually-installed units in `all`, report a listed-but-absent unit honestly
stories.goal: As the CIO doing maintenance or debugging on the Pi, I want ONE command I can run on the Pi to stop, start, restart, kill, or status any single OBD-project service OR ALL of them, so I can service the system or work through issues without hand-typing systemctl for each unit + remembering the full unit list.

filesActuallyTouched: src/pi/ops/unit_manifest.py (new -- THE unit SSOT: names, aliases, order, per-consumer policy)
src/pi/splash/service_control.py (SERVICE_ALLOWLIST now DERIVED from the manifest)
deploy/deploy-pi.sh (new step_install_obdctl + wired into the run sequence)
tests/deploy/obdctl_wrapper_sim.sh (new -- executes the real deploy step off-Pi)

stories.completionNotes:
IMPLEMENTED AS PYTHON, NOT BASH (AC-10 permits either: 'bash -n / shellcheck clean (or ruff if Python)'). Reason is AC-2: the ONLY way to have literally one list is for both consumers to import it. A bash obdctl would have had to parse a manifest or mirror it -- i.e. the second list the AC forbids. Python also gets the injectable-runner + honest-result idiom already established by US-403's service_control.py. It is stdlib-only and imports nothing from the app, and deploy points it at SYSTEM python3, NOT the venv: obdctl is the tool you reach for when the Pi is broken, and a half-installed venv is one of the things that can be broken (pinned by two tests).

SSOT DESIGN -- shared NAMES, separate POLICY. src/pi/ops/unit_manifest.py owns unit names/aliases/ordering; each entry carries `kioskVerbs` (default EMPTY) and service_control.SERVICE_ALLOWLIST is now `unit_manifest.kioskAllowlist()`. Because the default is empty, deriving the kiosk list from an 8-unit manifest still yields the SAME narrow 4-unit list US-403 shipped -- the splash, state server and boot-state emitter stay unreachable from the unprivileged kiosk, and the 51- polkit mirror stays valid. The pre-existing US-403 suite passes untouched, which is the proof of no widening. A new deploy test also asserts every kiosk-granted unit is named in the polkit rule, so a future `kioskVerbs` addition cannot ship a UI offering actions PolicyKit denies.

THE DERIVATION TEST IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. `assert derived == hardcoded` passes just as happily against a copy-paste -- it proves the values match today, never that one COMES FROM the other. It went green immediately on the unrefactored module. Rewrote it to perturb the manifest and reload service_control, watched it go RED (KeyError), then refactored. Same family as last sprint's CSS finding: asserting a rule EXISTS is not asserting it REACHES.

ORDERING IS GROUNDED, NOT INVENTED. Start order follows the units' own declarations read out of the unit files: rfcomm-bind (Requires=bluetooth.service) -> powerwatch -> eclipse-obd -> states-http -> boot-state (Wants=states-http) -> splash-boot (After=states-http+boot-state) -> splash-grace (After=states-http) -> dashboard (After=states-http). STOP_ORDER is that list reversed -- ONE ordering to keep correct -- which lands kiosk/splash first and the core obd/powerwatch last, exactly as AC-6 asks.

conditionalOutcome 2 DISCHARGED EMPIRICALLY, not by comment: eclipse-sync.service is kept in the manifest flagged installedByDeploy=False (so the US-403 allow-list + polkit rule are preserved byte-for-byte) but is excluded from `all`. A new test greps all three deploy installers (deploy-pi.sh + the splash and dashboard kit install.sh files) and confirms NONE installs it -- and asserts the converse for all 8 canonical units. The drift guard runs in BOTH directions on purpose: a one-way check lets the manifest rot silently on the side nobody asserts. Note the unit list was previously spread across those 3 files, which is why the SSOT had to exist.

JUDGEMENT CALL 1 -- DECLINED => EXIT 2. Refusing a confirm is not a failure, but the run did not do what the command line asked, and a script (or a half-read terminal) must not read a partial teardown as complete. So SKIPPED counts as incomplete. `SKIP` (a unit this Pi never had, inside `all`) does NOT -- nothing was requested of a unit that does not exist, so `stop all` on a Pi missing splash-grace still exits 0. Documented in --help and deploy/README.

JUDGEMENT CALL 2 -- DECLINING DURING `stop all` STOPS EVERYTHING EXCEPT THE GUARD, rather than aborting the whole batch. The operator asked for maintenance; the cardinal rule is only that powerwatch must not be left down. Confirmations are all collected BEFORE the first unit is touched, so a decline never strands a half-torn-down stack.

JUDGEMENT CALL 3 -- `kill` ALWAYS CONFIRMS (unless --yes). AC-5 allows 'confirm or explicit action word'; chose confirm because SIGKILL on a car computer is unrecoverable-in-kind. --yes keeps it scriptable. `kill` is never reached from a failed `stop` -- there is a test for that, since silently escalating would destroy the very state a clean stop was protecting.

HONESTY BUG CAUGHT BY RUNNING IT. Ran the CLI on this Windows host (no systemctl): every unit read `unknown` and the banner announced 'SAFE-SHUTDOWN GUARD IS DOWN'. `unknown` means the READ failed, not that the guard is down -- a confident wrong claim about the one unit whose status matters most, and an operator who chases a phantom outage once stops believing the banner the time it is real. Now `unknown` prints a distinct 'could not read / not confirmed down, not confirmed up' notice. Test added first. Same posture throughout: after-states are always re-read from systemctl, never inferred from a zero exit (a restart that returns 0 but leaves the unit `failed` reports FAIL).

DEPLOY STEP IS EXECUTED, NOT JUST GREPPED. The wrapper is written by a heredoc nested inside a double-quoted string that is itself sent over SSH -- a mis-escaped `$@` or a heredoc expanding on the wrong side would only surface on the Pi as `obdctl: not found`. tests/deploy/obdctl_wrapper_sim.sh runs the REAL step body off-Pi with `remote` and `sudo` stubbed, then executes the wrapper it produced and re-runs the step to prove idempotence. PASS.

GATES: 109 targeted tests green (tests/pi/ops/ 63 + tests/deploy/test_obdctl_install.py 17 + the pre-existing US-403 service_control 23 + states_http_service_control 6). ruff clean on all touched Python; `bash -n deploy/deploy-pi.sh` and `bash -n` on the sim both clean. HOST GAPS unchanged from last sprint: `make` is NOT on PATH here so `make lint` was run as its underlying `ruff check`; black + mypy are not installed on this host. shellcheck is not installed either (bash -n only) -- FOR PM: if CI has shellcheck/mypy, they are integration-time gates on deploy-pi.sh + src/pi/ops/. Full-suite regression is also a PM-time gate; service_control.py is a base module for the kiosk path, so prioritise it.

ON-PI VALIDATION OWED (all 5 validationCriteria are ON-PI-CLI-EXERCISE and none can be discharged from a dev box): after deploy, run `obdctl status all` (expect 8 units with live states), `obdctl restart obd`, `obdctl stop all` (watch the reverse order + the powerwatch prompt), `obdctl kill dashboard`, and `obdctl stop powerwatch` without --force. Worth watching specifically: whether splash-boot/splash-grace/rfcomm-bind read `inactive` in normal operation -- the manifest flags them inactiveIsNormal and the status line annotates them, and that annotation is a claim about real runtime behaviour that only the Pi can confirm. Also confirm sudo does not re-prompt for a password mid-`stop all`.

(obdctl restart obd  (alias)) → (eclipse-obd restarts; before->after state shown; exit 0)  [from US-492]
(obdctl stop all) → (stops the units in reverse-dependency order; powerwatch stop triggers the loud warning + confirm; summary table shows per-unit result)  [from US-492]
(obdctl kill dashboard) → (requires explicit intent, SIGKILLs the kiosk, reports killed + after-state inactive)  [from US-492]
(obdctl stop powerwatch  (without --force)) → (refuses/warns + requires confirm (safe-shutdown-guard protection); restart powerwatch is unrestricted)  [from US-492]
